why: The record's own gf_detail says "should not be considered safe for celiac diners", the cited article puts 麩 (wheat gluten) in the miso soup that comes with the plate, and the kitchen is one elderly cook running one fryer for croquettes, shrimp fry and cutlets. There is nothing here to ask FOR. Same consistency point as Grill Fukuya; low confidence if "ask" is the app's floor for unlabelled yoshoku.

quote: Salt-grilled (shio) skewers are seasoned only with Hakata salt rather than the wheat-containing tare, so the seasoning itself is wheat-free - but they share the grill with tare skewers, so this does not make them celiac-safe. Confirm directly with staff.
found: 「こちらでは備長炭を使用した炭火焼で伯方の塩を使用とのこと」 and 「せせり、程よい塩加減で炭火焼きの香ばしさがダイレクトに味に加わります」
method: plain fetch
note: 伯方の塩 is named on the page. Small correction: 伯方 is Hakata Island in the Seto Inland Sea (Ehime), a different Hakata from Fukuoka's — 'Hakata salt' reads as the Fukuoka one to an English reader. Otherwise exact, and the refusal to promote shio skewers to safe is the right call.
Three of four claims are supported verbatim by the correctly branch-matched article; the fourth is uncited and its evidence is on that same page. The strongest record in this shard.
